text_blocks.snippet: Da Nang is Vietnam’s vibrant coastal hub, offering a perfect mix of pristine beaches, lush mountain resorts, and ancient cultural sites. Key highlights include relaxing on My Khe Beach, exploring the spectacular Golden Bridge at Ba Na Hills, and taking day trips to the lantern-lit streets of nearby Hoi An. Travels with Ingrid +3
snippet_highlighted_words: relaxing on My Khe Beach, exploring the spectacular Golden Bridge at Ba Na Hills, and taking day trips to the lantern-lit streets of nearby Hoi An

list.snippet: Ba Na Hills & The Golden Bridge: Located about an hour outside the city, this mountaintop amusement park is famous for the Golden Bridge, a surreal pedestrian walkway cradled by two giant stone hands. Your admission ticket covers the scenic cable car ride and entry to the French Village and theme park areas. Travels with Ingrid +2
My Khe Beach: Stretch out on miles of soft white sand. It is an ideal spot for early morning swims, beginner surfing, or simply relaxing with a fresh coconut at a beach bar.

Marble Mountains: A cluster of five limestone and marble hills just south of the city center. You can hike the stone steps or take an elevator to explore secret cave shrines, hidden viewpoints, and natural open-air caves where sunlight pours in.

Lady Buddha & Son Tra Peninsula: Perched on the mountains of the Son Tra Peninsula, Linh Ung Pagoda is home to a massive 67-meter-tall Lady Buddha statue. The surrounding area offers panoramic ocean views and the chance to spot rare, endangered red-shanked douc langur monkeys. Tripadvisor +1

Dragon Bridge Fire Show: You cannot miss this iconic bridge shaped like a dragon. If you are visiting on a weekend (typically Friday, Saturday, and Sunday nights at 9:00 PM), head to the riverfront to watch the dragon breathe massive plumes of fire and water. Little Birdie Travel +1

list.snippet: Han River Promenade: Stroll along the riverfront in the evening to see the city lights and pass by the heart-shaped lanterns of the Love Bridge. Travels with Ingrid +1

Seafood & Local Markets: Treat yourself to a fresh seafood dinner along the beach road, or dive into local street food. Do not leave without trying local favorites like Mi Quang (turmeric noodles) and Banh Xeo (crispy Vietnamese pancakes). Hayley on Holiday +1

Café Culture: Da Nang has a thriving coffee scene. Whether you are looking for a minimalist specialty roaster or a tranquil garden café surrounded by koi ponds, you will find plenty of spots to relax. Travels with Ingrid +1
Hoi An Ancient Town: Just a 40-minute drive south, this UNESCO World Heritage site is famous for its preserved yellow merchant houses, lantern-lined streets, and riverside dining. Facebook
